chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ:

translations.en: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān narrated from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنْ رَجُلَيْنِ كَانَ لَهُمَا مَالٌ مِنْهُ بِأَيْدِيهِمَا وَ مِنْهُ مُتَفَرِّقٌ عَنْهُمَا فَاقْتَسَمَا بِالسَّوِيَّةِ مَا كَانَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمَا وَ مَا كَانَ غَائِبًا فَهَلَكَ نَصِيبُ أَحَدِهِمَا مِمَّا كَانَ عَنْهُ غَائِبًا وَ اسْتَوْفَى الْآخَرُ أَ يَرُدُّ عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ

translations.en: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about two men who had wealth, some of it in their hands and some of it dispersed away from them. They divided equally what was in their hands and what was absent, then the share of one of them from what had been absent was lost, while the other fully received his. Should he return something to his companion?
He عليه السلام said: "Yes; he must not take away his companion’s wealth."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about jointly owned wealth that was divided before all of it had been collected. If one partner receives his absent share while the other partner’s absent share is lost, the one who received must return to his companion so that one party does not exclusively retain the wealth. The narration reflects the principle of fairness and preservation of shared financial rights.
en.seo_question: If two partners divide joint wealth equally and one later loses his absent share, must the other compensate him?

key_terms.مَالٌ: wealth or property jointly possessed by the two men
key_terms.بِأَيْدِيهِمَا: in their possession or under their control
key_terms.مُتَفَرِّقٌ: dispersed or located away from immediate possession
key_terms.غَائِبًا: absent property not presently in hand
